snapshot.what_it_does: Infosys Limited provides AI-first business consulting and technology services, enabling organizations to unlock AI value at scale through its AI-first value framework, deep domain expertise, and orchestration of an AI-native partner ecosystem. With over four decades of experience, it helps clients ideate, plan and execute their journey to an AI-first future, supported by services brands like Infosys Topaz (AI), Cobalt (cloud) and Aster (marketing).

segments.name: Retail, Consumer Packaged Goods, Transportation and Logistics
Others (India, Japan, China, Infosys Public Services, other public services enterprises)

snapshot.geographies: Incorporated and domiciled in India (registered office: Electronics City, Bengaluru); listed on BSE, NSE and NYSE (ADS). Two major tax jurisdictions are India and the United States, with tax returns filed in other overseas jurisdictions; go-to-market units include India, Japan and China. Segment revenue shares by geography are not stated.
key_facts: FY2026 revenue of ₹1,78,650 crore (US$20,158 million), crossing the US$20 billion mark with 9.6% growth Y-o-Y in ₹ and 3.1% CC growth
FY2026 net profit of ₹29,440 crore (US$3,313 million); basic EPS ₹71.58
Adjusted operating margin of 21.0%; free cash flow of ₹33,097 crore (US$3.7 billion) with 112.3% FCF conversion of net profit
Large deal TCV of US$14.9 billion (net new 55%); 88 clients with US$50 million+ revenue
Returned over US$4 billion to shareholders via dividends (US$2.1 billion) and buybacks (US$2 billion); total dividend ₹48 per share; ₹18,000 crore buyback at ₹1,800 per share

promised_vs_delivered.verdict: Mixed credibility: margin guidance (20-22%) has been consistently held and AI revenue growth promises were exceeded, but FY27 revenue guidance was cut twice within two quarters (1.5-3.5% to 1-2%). Management is reliable on margins and AI traction, less so on topline forecasting.

8,000 graduates hired in Q2 FY27; ~20,000 full-year target reiterated (Q2 FY27 call); FY27 incomplete

bull.point: Revenue momentum accelerating: Q1 FY27 +14.0% YoY, Q2 FY27 +10.7%; FY26 revenue ₹1,78,650 crore (US$20.16bn), +9.6% YoY, crossing US$20 billion.
AI revenue scaling ahead of promise: AI-first share rose from 5.5% (Q3 FY26) to 10.5% (Q2 FY27), +29% QoQ; large deal TCV US$14.9 billion.
Strong cash and returns: FCF ₹33,097 crore with 112.3% conversion of net profit; over US$4 billion returned via dividends and ₹18,000 crore buyback; margin band 20-22% held.

bear.point: FY27 revenue guidance cut twice within two quarters: 1.5-3.5% CC to 1.5-3% to 1-2%; original range abandoned, topline forecasting unreliable.
Manufacturing headwind confirmed: offshoring plus exited European manufacturing deal impacted growth guidance by ~2%; segment figures not stated.
Profit volatility: Q3 FY26 PAT fell 2.2% YoY despite +8.9% revenue; Q2 FY27 PAT growth decelerated to 6.2% from 12.3% in Q1; EBITDA margin compressed from 24.2% to 23.4-23.7%.

watch: Whether FY27 1-2% CC revenue guidance holds or is cut a third time at the Q3 FY27 call.
AI revenue share trajectory beyond 10.5% and whether the mega deal delivers >1% growth contribution in FY28 as promised.
H2 compensation hikes (October/January) impact on the 20-22% margin band, and progress toward ~20,000 graduate hires (8,000 done by Q2).
